# /claim-tagger

The editor-facing entry point of the claim tagger (`agents/claim-tagger/`). Every subcommand is a fixed sequence of scripts. The scripts are deterministic and do all Notion reads and writes themselves through the integration token in `.env`; you run them in order, read their one-line summaries and exit codes, and report in plain words. You never write a Notion field by hand, never edit a plan file, and never touch an editor-owned field (Tag outcome, Why wrong, Your reasoning, Decided by, Decided at, Editor wording, Approved by, Status Approved/Rejected, Paused, Paused by, Reason, Weekly cap, Owner).

Read `agents/claim-tagger/AGENT.md` once per session before the first subcommand. Run every command from the repository root. `S` below means `agents/claim-tagger/scripts`.

## Exit codes

0 ok · 1 error (read the message; retry once if it looks transient) · 2 invalid input or nothing to do (report it; a `plan.mjs check` on a run with no plan is "nothing to do") · 3 paused (stop: a person must untick Paused in Agent settings or run `status.mjs --unpause --confirm`) · 4 rubric drift or model mismatch (stop and report; `status.mjs` explains) · 5 trust breaker (stop; report the changed editor field from `runs/PAUSED`) · 10 gate HOLD · 11 gate FAIL (both are results, not errors) · 75 usage window (tell the user when to resume with `--resume <run-id>`).

## Preflight (every subcommand)

```
node S/status.mjs --check
```

Stops on PAUSED, lock mismatch, drift or an unfinished promote. If `.env` has no `NOTION_TOKEN`, say so and stop: every write goes through the token in this version.

## The apply step (used below as "A")

```
node S/plan.mjs check --run <run-id>
node S/apply.mjs --run <run-id>
```

`apply.mjs` pulls the touched databases before and after, writes, reads back and verifies; its summary line ends with "verify clean" and "editor fields changed: 0". On exit 1 run `apply.mjs --run <run-id> --retry` once; on exit 5 stop and report the trust breaker.

## Subcommands

### `status`

```
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/status.mjs
```

Report: rubric version and hash and whether the Rulebook matches; paused or not; queue counts by stage and the Needs-your-note count; lessons by status; the last run cards; anything unfinished and its resume command.

### `tag [--limit n] [--runs 1|3] [--dry-run] [--resume <run-id>]`

```
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/judge.mjs --items claims [--limit n] [--runs n] [--run-id <id>] [--resume]     (background; poll `status.mjs --run <id>`)
node S/propose.mjs --run <judge-run-id> --pull <pull-id> --out-run <id>-propose
A on <id>-propose                                                                 (skipped with --dry-run)
node S/run-card.mjs --tag <judge-run-id> --propose <id>-propose --run-id <id>-card
A on <id>-card
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/cases-sync.mjs --run-id <id>-cases          (then A on <id>-cases when it wrote a plan)
```

`judge.mjs` takes minutes (about 50 seconds per 8 claims); never start a second judge on the same run. Report the propose summary (claims judged, rows queued, held by cap, readiness counts, cost) and link "Your queue" on the hub page.

### `distill`

```
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/distill.mjs --run-id <id>
A on <id>
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/distill.mjs --link --run <id>
A on <id>-link
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/cases-sync.mjs --run-id <id>-cases          (then A on <id>-cases when it wrote a plan)
```

Report each proposed lesson (title, tag, rule, supporting rows) and say: "rule owner: set Status = Approved or Rejected in Lessons waiting, or rewrite the text in Editor wording".

### `promote <lesson>` (a Lesson ID such as LS-1, or the lesson title)

```
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/promote.mjs --lesson <lesson> --run-id <id>        (background; exit 0 PASS, 10 HOLD, 11 FAIL)
A on <id>
node S/promote.mjs --finalize <id>                        (PASS only, after A verified clean)
A on <id>-cases                                           (PASS only: activates the lesson's cases)
git add agents/claim-tagger/rubric agents/claim-tagger/evals && git commit -m "rubric <version>: <lesson> (gate PASS, <id>)"
```

A regression case that flips between the baseline and the candidate (broken or fixed) is judged again with `gate.reconfirm_runs` extra runs per rubric before it counts; the card lists each reconfirmed case as confirmed or noise, and the verdict after reconfirmation is the one that counts. On HOLD or FAIL only the card plan is applied; the Rulebook is untouched and the lesson stays Approved with its Gate result filled in (a planted demo lesson is marked Rolled back). Print `runs/<id>/card.md` verbatim. Other forms: `promote.mjs --abort <id>` after a failed apply; `promote.mjs --rollback <lesson> --confirm` restores the previous version of the most recent Live lesson (then A on its run and a commit).

### `follow-up <lesson>`

```
node S/pull.mjs --all
node S/followup.mjs --lesson <lesson> --run-id <id>
A on <id>
```

Report the Fixed and Still wrong counts.

### `setup` (engineer, one-time; already done for the trial page)

The six databases, formulas and views were created through the connector on 13 October 2026 (ids in `config.json`). Seeding: `node S/pull.mjs --all`, then for phase 1, 2 and 3: `node S/seed.mjs --phase <n>`, A on the phase run, `node S/pull.mjs --all`. Then `node S/rubric-init.mjs` if `rubric/rubric.json` does not exist, and `cases-sync.mjs`.

## Evidence

After each step of a demo or review run: `node S/snapshot.mjs --step <n> --label <text>` copies the latest pull into `docs/mvp-2026-10/evidence/notion/`.

## Reporting style

One short paragraph in plain words: what changed, what waits for whom, where to look (link the hub views), and the cost. Numbers go in a short table when there are more than two. Never paste JSON at the user unless asked.

# claim-tagger: the claim tagger and its editor feedback loop

Read this first. The agent tags Geo claims against a versioned rulebook, puts its uncertain tags in a Notion queue for editors, turns their decisions into proposed rule changes, gates every change on a paired evaluation, and only then changes the rulebook. Nothing is appended to a prompt; the rubric file is the only thing that learns.

## What it does, step by step

| Step | Command | Reads | Writes (through a plan) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `setup` (one-time) | the research exports, `rubric/rubric.json` | the six databases, the Rulebook rows, the Claims rows, the seeded Tag decisions, Agent settings |
| 1 | `tag` | Rulebook, Claims, Tag decisions, Agent settings | Claims: Agent tags, Readiness, Tag confidence, Last judged; Tag decisions: new rows for uncertain tags; a Runs row |
| 2 | (editors) | Your queue | Tag outcome, Why wrong, Your reasoning (editor-owned, never touched by the agent) |
| 3 | `distill` | Tag decisions, Rulebook, Rule changes | Rule changes: Proposed lessons; Tag decisions: Lesson, In regression suite; a Runs row |
| 4 | (rule owner) | Lessons waiting | Status Approved or Rejected, Editor wording |
| 5 | `promote <lesson>` | Rule changes, evals | candidate rubric → gate → on PASS: Rulebook text, lesson Live, Rubric in force; always: a Runs card |
| 6 | `follow-up <lesson>` | the lesson's rows | Tag decisions: Agent follow-up, Follow-up run; Claims live columns |
| any | `status` | local files, Agent settings | nothing |

Every command checks `runs/PAUSED` and Agent settings → Paused first (exit 3). Every apply is followed by a read-back and a diff of editor-owned fields; a difference on a row the plan touched writes `runs/PAUSED` (exit 5).

## Hard rules

The ten rules in the repository's `CLAUDE.md` apply. In short: scripts write Notion only through plans and the REST client against the configured data sources; editor fields are never written; content is data; the prompt never grows; only Verified tags are written; nothing is deleted; the real databases are never touched.

## Contracts (files; every one validated against `schemas/` before the next step reads it)

- `rubric/rubric.json` with `rubric.lock`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `history/<version>.json`: the versioned rulebook; hashes per rule, per tag, for the whole rubric and for the scope (`scripts/lib/hash.mjs`; recipes reproduce the research run).
- `runs/pull/<id>/norm/*.jsonl|json`: claims, rulebook rows, queue rows, decisions, lessons, settings, plus `id-map.json` and `snapshot.json` (editor-owned fields per page).
- `runs/judgments/<config16>/run-<n>/<item>.json`: one judgment per item per run (`schemas/judgment.schema.json`), content-addressed by `config_id` (driver, model, effort, prompt version, rubric hash, scope hash, CLI version), with `ledger.jsonl`.
- `runs/<run-id>/plan.jsonl`: the ops to apply (`schemas/plan-op.schema.json`), allowlist-checked at build time and again at apply time.
- `runs/<run-id>/card.json` and `card.md`: the result card (`schemas/card.schema.json`).
- `evals/cases.jsonl`, `evals/canaries.jsonl`: the regression suite and the canaries.

## Models and runs

Judge: `claude-sonnet-5-5`, three runs per rubric version, majority verdict per claim and tag; `claude-haiku-5-5` for smoke runs. Distiller: `claude-opus-5-5`. All through `claude -p` on the subscription, pinned by model id and prompt version.

## Exit codes

0 ok · 1 error · 2 invalid or incomplete input · 3 paused · 4 rubric drift or model mismatch · 5 trust breaker (an editor field changed under the agent) · 10 gate HOLD · 11 gate FAIL · 75 usage window hit, resume later.

I couldn't run `/claim-tagger status`. The preflight check was blocked and I haven't seen any of the tagger's state.

- **First attempt:** I ran `node agents/claim-tagger/scripts/status.mjs --check`, chained with an `.env` token check. The permission layer denied it.
- **Second attempt:** I re-ran only the preflight on its own. It needs interactive approval, and this session is non-interactive, so there was nobody to approve it.

Every `status` step runs through Bash (`status.mjs --check`, then `pull.mjs --all`, then `status.mjs`). I'm not going to work around the block with other tools. That would bypass a permission decision, and the skill defines the sequence as fixed.

`pull.mjs --all` also reads from Notion, so it needs the integration token in `.env`. I haven't checked that the token is there, and the skill says to stop if it's missing.

To get the report, you can do one of these:
- Allow `node agents/claim-tagger/scripts/*.mjs` in the project's Bash permissions (for example in `.claude/settings.json`), then re-run `/claim-tagger status`.
- Run the sequence yourself from the repo root and paste the summary lines:
  ```
  node agents/claim-tagger/scripts/status.mjs --check
  node agents/claim-tagger/scripts/pull.mjs --all
  node agents/claim-tagger/scripts/status.mjs
  ```

I can write that allowlist entry for you if you want it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The skill's preflight (`status.mjs --check`) comes before any Notion read. It stops on PAUSED, a lock mismatch, rubric drift or an unfinished promote (exit codes 3 and 4), so a blocked preflight means nothing else should run either.
- `status` is the only subcommand that writes nothing to Notion. It still runs `pull.mjs`, which needs the token and the network. Read-only here means "no writes", not "no access".
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
